title: Division always makes smaller
statement: Dividing always gives a result smaller than the number you started with, so dividing by a fraction cannot make a number bigger.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict whether a quotient will be larger or smaller than the dividend, without calculating
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts the quotient of a number divided by a proper fraction is smaller than the number

example.item: Without calculating, is 6 / 1/2 more or less than 6?

evidence_patterns.item_shape: evaluate a whole number divided by a unit fraction
evidence_patterns.signature: halves the number instead of doubling it

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is one wrong prediction. The belief is stated as a rule ('dividing makes it smaller') and holds for decimals too; it often coexists with math.frac.multiply-makes-bigger.

vs.math.frac.invert-dividend: Ask the learner to predict before calculating. Procedure bugs give a wrong number but often a correct prediction of direction; this belief gets the direction wrong.
vs.math.frac.division-is-sharing-only: Sharing-only believers say 6 / 1/2 'makes no sense' or reinterpret it; this belief answers confidently with a smaller number.

conflicts_with.label: CCSS 5.NF.B.7: divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions

resolved_by.label: CCSS 5.NF.B.7: divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions
CCSS 6.NS.A.1: interpret and compute quotients of fractions

sources.citation: Fischbein, E., Deri, M., Nello, M. S., & Marino, M. S. (1985). The role of implicit models in solving verbal problems in multiplication and division. Journal for Research in Mathematics Education, 16(1), 3-17.
sources.note: Implicit partitive model of division: the quotient must be smaller than the dividend.
